subject: FRE
label: Grade 03
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 03 French, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Presenting a friend
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Presenting a friend', you learn to describe a friend. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Presenting a friend' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: describe a friend, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: 'Il s'appelle [prénom]. Il a dix ans. Il est egyptien. Il aime le football.' Method: Model run for 'Presenting a friend'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Describe a friend: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Present your friend with name and age. Voici mon ami [prénom]. [Here is my friend (name).] Il a huit ans. [He is eight years old.] Voici mon amie [prénom]. [Here is my friend (name).] Elle a neuf ans. [She is nine years old.] Use il for a boy and elle for a girl.

Step 2, Describe what he or she looks like. Mon ami est grand et il a les cheveux noirs. [My friend is tall and has black hair.] Mon amie est petite et elle a les yeux bleus. [My friend is small and has blue eyes.] Notice petite takes an e because my friend is a girl.

Step 3, Describe character and likes. Mon ami est gentil et drôle. [My friend is kind and funny.] Il aime le football. [He likes football.] Mon amie est sportive. [My friend is sporty.] Elle aime la danse. [She likes dancing.] Add one thing you do together.

Step 4, A short dialogue. Maman : Comment est ton ami ? [What is your friend like?] L'enfant : Il est grand et très sympa. [He is tall and very nice.] Maman : Comment s'appelle-t-il ? [What is his name?] L'enfant : Il s'appelle [prénom]. [His name is (name).]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says Mon amie est grand. Correction: Mon amie est grande, because my friend is a girl and the adjective adds an e. Another slip is Il a neuf ans for a girl who is nine; say Elle a neuf ans.

Step 6, Your turn: present a boy friend, ten years old, short, kind, who likes drawing. Model answer: Voici mon ami. Il a dix ans. Il est petit et gentil. Il aime dessiner. [Here is my friend. He is ten. He is small and kind. He likes drawing.]

modules.title: The verbs to have and to be
modules.intro: In this unit, 'The verbs to have and to be', you learn to use avoir and etre. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'The verbs to have and to be' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: use avoir and etre, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: etre: je suis, tu es, il est. avoir: j'ai, tu as, il a. 'Je suis grand. J'ai un chat.' Method: Model run for 'The verbs to have and to be'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Use avoir and etre: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Learn avoir [to have]: j'ai, tu as, il a, elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont, elles ont. Example: J'ai un frère. [I have a brother.] Nous avons un chat. [We have a cat.] Say the full row aloud with a pointing finger.

Step 2, Learn être [to be]: je suis, tu es, il est, elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont, elles sont. Example: Je suis content. [I am happy.] Elles sont à l'école. [They are at school.] Say the full row aloud.

Step 3, Choose between them. Use être for what someone is: Il est grand. [He is tall.] Use avoir for age and possessions: J'ai dix ans. [I am ten.] Elle a une bicyclette. [She has a bicycle.] Make three sentences with each verb.

Step 4, Dialogue. Élève A : Tu as quel âge ? [How old are you?] Élève B : J'ai neuf ans. Et toi ? [I am nine. And you?] Élève A : J'ai dix ans. Nous sommes amis ! [I am ten. We are friends!] Élève B : Oui, nous sommes dans la même classe. [Yes, we are in the same class.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says Je suis dix ans. Correction: J'ai dix ans. Another says Il a content. Correction: Il est content. Also keep ont and sont apart: Ils ont un chat [They have a cat] but Ils sont contents [They are happy].

Step 6, Your turn: write about yourself using three forms of avoir and three of être. Model answer: Je suis [mon prénom]. J'ai huit ans. Mon frère a six ans. Nous sommes contents. Ils sont gentils. [I am (my name). I am eight. My brother is six. We are happy. They are kind.]

modules.title: Adjectives and plural
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Adjectives and plural', you learn to use simple adjectives and plurals. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Adjectives and plural' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: use simple adjectives and plurals, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: un petit chat, une petite chatte. Plural: add -s (les chats noirs). Feminine usually adds -e. Method: Model run for 'Adjectives and plural'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Use simple adjectives and plurals: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Feminine adds an e. grand [tall, masculine] becomes grande [feminine]; petit becomes petite; content becomes contente; vert becomes verte. Say each pair aloud and listen for the final consonant. In petit the t is silent, in petite it is heard.

Step 2, Plural adds an s. un chat noir [a black cat] becomes des chats noirs [black cats]. une maison blanche [a white house] becomes des maisons blanches [white houses]. The adjective agrees in gender and number with the noun.

Step 3, Put it in position. Many short, common adjectives go before the noun: un petit chat, une grande maison, un bon livre. Colour adjectives go after: un chat noir, une voiture rouge. Say these four phrases aloud with their pictures.

Step 4, Describe a picture. Voici une petite maison blanche. [Here is a small white house.] Il y a deux grands arbres verts. [There are two tall green trees.] Dans le jardin, il y a des chats noirs. [In the garden there are black cats.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says des chats noir. Correction: des chats noirs, because chats is plural. Another says une maison petit. Correction: une petite maison; the adjective must be feminine and goes before maison.

Step 6, Your turn: describe two girls who are tall and kind, and a small black dog. Model answer: Les filles sont grandes et gentilles. J'ai un petit chien noir. [The girls are tall and kind. I have a small black dog.] Check each adjective ending.

modules.title: Free time and hobbies
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Free time and hobbies', you learn to talk about hobbies. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Free time and hobbies' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: talk about hobbies, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: 'J'aime jouer au football et lire. Le week-end, je nage.' Method: Model run for 'Free time and hobbies'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Talk about hobbies: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Say what you like to do. J'aime jouer au football. [I like to play football.] J'aime lire. [I like to read.] J'aime dessiner. [I like to draw.] After j'aime we use the infinitive, the form ending in er, ir or re.

Step 2, Use jouer à and faire de. Je joue au tennis. [I play tennis.] Je joue à la balle. [I play with a ball.] Je fais du vélo. [I ride a bike.] Je fais de la natation. [I swim.] à plus le becomes au; de plus le becomes du.

Step 3, Say how often and when. Le samedi, je joue avec mes amis. [On Saturdays I play with my friends.] Le soir, je lis un livre. [In the evening I read a book.] Je regarde la télé le dimanche. [I watch TV on Sundays.]

Step 4, Dialogue. Élève A : Qu'est-ce que tu fais le week-end ? [What do you do at the weekend?] Élève B : Je fais du vélo avec mon père. [I ride my bike with my father.] Élève A : Moi, je joue au foot. [I play football.] Élève B : On peut jouer ensemble ! [We can play together!]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says Je joue le football. Correction: Je joue au football. Another says Je fais le vélo. Correction: Je fais du vélo. Remember that these verbs need à or de before the activity.

Step 6, Your turn: write three sentences about your hobbies using jouer, faire and aimer. Model answer: Je joue au basket. Je fais de la danse. J'aime lire des histoires. [I play basketball. I do dance. I like reading stories.]

ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
